key_insight: Large-scale video generation models encode rich, implicit 3D and physical priors that can be extracted and repurposed to give multimodal systems fine-grained spatial reasoning without requiring explicit 3D data.
problem_solved: Addresses the spatial blindness of multimodal models — their inability to perform reliable geometric reasoning and physical-dynamic inference — while avoiding reliance on scarce or hard-to-generalize explicit 3D supervision.
method: Probe and extract implicit spatial priors from pretrained video/generative models (e.g., by analyzing latent trajectories, multi-frame consistency, or learned motion/depth cues).
Distill these priors into compact modules or adapters that augment perception/LLM stacks for tasks like depth estimation, occlusion reasoning, and physical prediction.
Validate via downstream scene-understanding benchmarks, showing improved geometric accuracy and generalization without explicit multi-view or 3D training data.
impact: Enables stronger geometric and physical reasoning for vision-language systems and robotics while reducing dependence on costly 3D data—facilitating more robust scene understanding in real-world and low-data settings.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: pretrained video generator → spatial-prior extraction → adapter → downstream tasks (depth, occlusion, dynamics).
Before/after examples: original image vs. inferred depth/occlusion overlays and predicted physical trajectories.
Bar chart: performance comparison on geometric benchmarks (baseline multimodal vs. augmented-with-priors).
Icon strip: benefits — less 3D data, better generalization, real-time adaptation, broader task coverage.
paper_title: Generation Models Know Space: Unleashing Implicit 3D Priors for Scene Understanding
paper_authors: Xianjin Wu, Dingkang Liang, Tianrui Feng, Kui Xia, Yumeng Zhang
